issue.body: ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/nifty-ioana-9rdm6g ### To Reproduce 1. Create a root `global-error.tsx` file 2. Throw an error in the root layout but in a nested route that exists, say `/signin` 3. Start the application with `next start` (not dev mode) 4. Navigate to `/signin` and see that `global-error.tsx` is unused, and instead the default Next "Application error" page appears 5. If I create a `global-error.tsx` file next to the nested layout page (see `app/sample-page/unused-global-error.tsx` in the CodeSandbox) it will correctly show the error page. ### Current vs. Expected behavior When the Root Layout throws an error, the **current behavior** is to show the `global-error.tsx` at the same segment of the target route. If no `global-error.tsx` file exists for that route, Next's default "Application Error: a server-side exception occurred" page appears. My expected behavior would be to look for that route's `global-error.tsx` file (like it does now), and if it does not find it, use the root `global-error.tsx` (not doing it, it's defaulting to Next's default server-error page). ### Verify canary release - [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release ### Provide environment information ```bash Operating System: Platform: linux Arch: x64 Version: #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sun Aug 6 20:05:33 UTC 2023 Binaries: Node: 16.17.0 npm: 8.15.0 Yarn: 1.22.19 pnpm: 7.1.0 Relevant Packages: next: 13.5.1-canary.1 eslint-config-next: N/A react: 18.2.0 react-dom: 18.2.0 typescript: 5.2.2 Next.js Config: output: N/A ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) App Router, Routing (next/router, next/navigation, next/link) ### Additional context #52993 appears to be closely related but they describe the error happening in dev mode as well.

issue.title: Display global-error along dev overlay during development
issue.body:
### What

Display `global-error.js` along with error overlay in development. When a runtime error occurred, you should be able to view the  `global-error.js` content by just hiding the error overlay.


### Why

Current behavior of `global-error.js` confused a lot of users that it only renders in production build, howerver in dev it's always shows the error overlay. This was considered "expected" before as you should focus on fixing error in dev. But this brings a lot of inconvenience for users, since they can't view the `global-error.js` easily in development but production build.


#### After
The global-error content is displayed in the html with error overlay covered
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58fd73f8-7634-4a52-b6f8-c912cbb36fc3)

#### Before
Notice nothing displayed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/319f3eb0-5d30-4c51-8e29-872aaec42261)


Fixes #55462
Fixes #52993
Closes NDX-694
